displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that some moral propositions are best understood as truth-apt, defeasibly justified, and invariant under changes in individual or collective attitudes, which provides proportionate support for objective moral facts.

novelty.explanation: This integrates the realist definition, semantic evidence, and appearance-based epistemology while adding explicit defeasibility and a proportionate conclusion.

premises.text: Certain moral judgments retain their apparent correctness when approval, belief, sentiment, convention, and personal advantage are varied independently, providing defeasible evidence that their content is not fixed by those attitudes.

novelty.explanation: This develops the attitude-variation test while carefully treating its verdict as defeasible evidence rather than immediate proof.

premises.text: Moral clauses support assertion, negation, uncertainty, embedding, deliberation, and disagreement in ways that are economically explained by propositionally structured and truth-assessable content.

novelty.explanation: This broadens the transcript’s semantic tests into a cumulative explanatory argument without claiming that embedding alone establishes realism.

premises.text: Intellectual appearances can confer initial justification when they are clear, stable under reflection, mutually coherent, and not defeated by credible evidence of distortion, disagreement, or unreliable formation.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the unrestricted appeal to appearances by adding explicit quality conditions and defeater sensitivity.

premises.text: Disagreement and cultural influence reduce confidence only to the extent that they indicate unreliability; they do not automatically cancel every appearance, especially where reflection reveals shared thin evaluative structure.

novelty.explanation: This answers the disagreement and training objections without denying their legitimate evidential significance.

premises.text: If a moral proposition has truth-assessable content, is justified through undefeated evidence, and remains valid across stipulated changes in relevant attitudes, then treating it as objectively true is explanatorily warranted.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explicit bridge principle connecting semantics, epistemic justification, and attitude invariance to a restrained realist conclusion.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, the convergence of semantic behavior, undefeated intellectual appearance, and attitude invariance gives defeasible reason to accept at least some objective moral facts, without claiming certainty or universal agreement.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the live route while limiting the conclusion to defeasible support for at least some objective moral facts.

newArguments.title: Cross-perspectival error correction
newArguments.text: A moral practice can contain perspective-transcending standards when participants treat some changes of attitude as improvement and others as corruption. If every evaluative standard were fixed solely by current attitudes, the distinction between correcting an attitude and merely replacing it would become difficult to explain. Practices of giving reasons, exposing factual mistakes, testing consistency, and widening attention suggest that moral reflection aims at standards not exhausted by whichever response presently dominates. This does not prove robust realism, but it supplies an additional explanatory consideration for limited attitude-independent correctness.

novelty.explanation: This is a new explanatory argument from the internal role of correction and improvement in moral reflection.

newArguments.title: Defeater-sensitive convergence
newArguments.text: The epistemic case improves when intuitions are not counted indiscriminately. Begin with diverse judgments, disclose framing, separate semantic from normative questions, expose participants to counterarguments, and examine which verdicts converge after factual correction and perspective taking. Convergence under procedures designed to remove known distortions would not guarantee objectivity, yet it would answer the charge that realism relies only on private specialist phenomenology. The method converts intuitionism into a publicly criticizable research program whose outputs receive weight in proportion to their stability, independence, and resistance to identified defeaters.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the public-evidence weakness by proposing a transparent method for testing and weighting appearances.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that ordinary moral thought and communication do not presently warrant commitment to stance-independent facts because their semantics and intuitive support remain context-sensitive, disputed, and underdetermined.

novelty.explanation: This consolidates quietist semantics and the public-justification objection into a restrained anti-realist thesis about warranted commitment.

premises.text: Ordinary speakers can competently assert, contest, and act upon moral claims while lacking stable answers to technical questions distinguishing realism, error theory, relativism, and expressivism.

novelty.explanation: This develops the separation between practical linguistic competence and determinate theoretical metaethical commitment.

premises.text: Survey answers are unreliable indicators of folk metaethics unless instruments distinguish normative conviction, epistemic confidence, interpersonal disagreement, and claims about stance-independent truth.

novelty.explanation: This sharpens the methodological objection by specifying distinctions that a valid measurement design must preserve.

premises.text: A contextual account can treat moral utterances as assertions within practical and social frameworks while allowing their theoretical commitments to vary with conversational purpose, background assumptions, and inferential role.

novelty.explanation: This repairs quietism’s underdefinition by identifying concrete contextual determinants and preserving assertoric function.

premises.text: Intellectual appearances provide limited dialectical evidence when sincere, competent participants report absent or conflicting seemings and credible formation histories involving language, culture, pedagogy, and prior theory remain unresolved.

novelty.explanation: This combines interpersonal disagreement with a qualified genealogical defeater rather than assuming that either alone disproves realism.

premises.text: When several semantic and epistemic models explain the available discourse and phenomenology comparably well, suspension of stance-independent commitment is rational until discriminating evidence favors the realist model.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an underdetermination principle that yields suspension rather than treating the absence of decisive proof as proof of anti-realism.

conclusion.text: Therefore, moral practice may remain meaningful, reason-guided, and practically important while commitment to objective moral facts is withheld pending clearer semantics and publicly assessable evidence that discriminates among rival explanations.

novelty.explanation: This produces a proportionate quietist conclusion that preserves moral practice without claiming that objective facts are impossible.

newArguments.title: Model underdetermination test
newArguments.text: Competing metaethical models should be compared by predictions rather than by whether their vocabulary feels natural. Construct cases involving embedding, retraction, cross-context disagreement, motivational variation, and attitude change, then ask what each theory predicts about interpretation and behavior. If realism, contextual quietism, and sophisticated expressivism accommodate the same observations through comparable adjustments, those observations underdetermine the ontology. The appropriate result is not a declaration that realism is false, but disciplined suspension combined with a demand for evidence that one model predicts more accurately, explains more simply, or integrates better with independently supported psychology and linguistics.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a comparative model-selection framework for converting quietism from a possibility claim into a testable research strategy.

newArguments.title: Authority without metaphysical independence
newArguments.text: Practical authority may arise from relations among agents rather than from stance-independent properties. Vulnerability, reciprocity, dependence, bargaining constraints, and the need for justifiable common rules can generate reasons that no individual preference controls, even though those reasons remain grounded in human practices and conditions. Such authority can criticize immediate desires because it appeals to stable higher-order commitments and terms others could reasonably accept. This framework answers the claim that subjectivity reduces morality to momentary preference satisfaction while avoiding the further conclusion that authoritative reasons must exist independently of every possible evaluative stance.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the anti-realist authority account by supplying interpersonal and higher-order standards beyond immediate personal preference.
